claims.claim: Small model + strict JSON schema + batching cuts unit cost by >80%
claims.measured: Sonnet write-up → Haiku schema -99.4% (Batch API price of the Haiku schema version: $0.094/1k, computed, not run). The four cells: without / Sonnet 5.5 $29.50/1k; without / Haiku 5.5 $1.25/1k; with / Sonnet 5.5 $3.77/1k; with / Haiku 5.5 $0.188/1k. Write-up → schema on the same model -87.2% (Sonnet) / -84.9% (Haiku); Sonnet → Haiku with the schema -95.0%
claims.note: The cut clears 80% before any batch discount; each step clears it on its own (write-up → schema on either model, and Sonnet → Haiku). Batching was priced at 50%, not run. No write-up reached its 8,192-token cap (0 of 144 runs truncated).

claims.measured: fields correct of 126 (items fully correct of 36). With vs without, same model: Sonnet 126 (36) vs 69 (6); Haiku 120 (33) vs 69 (3). With the improvement, Haiku vs Sonnet: 120 (90–98%) vs 126 (97–100%), items 33 vs 36
claims.note: With the improvement every field and item count is at least the write-up's on the same model. The write-up prompt never lists the allowed labels, so a write-up's score counts the fields where one allowed label can be read off it (usable as a classification), read by a blind reader model (`claude-opus-5-5`, one pass). On the "with" row the Haiku version matched 6 fewer of 126 fields than the Sonnet version (−4.8 points), all on 2 tickets (tkt-01, tkt-02); the 95% Wilson intervals overlap. Implicit-row rule: no clear loss is detected (the intervals overlap), but the Haiku point estimates are lower and 36 runs cannot exclude a loss.

Sonnet with vs without: accuracy 4.17, coverage 3.42, actionability 3.08; serious errors 0.00/draft; core facts 94/96, detail facts 94/120 vs accuracy 3.92, coverage 5.00, actionability 3.42; serious errors 0.42/draft; core facts 95/96, detail facts 120/120. With the template, Haiku vs Sonnet: accuracy 3.83, coverage 3.58, actionability 2.67; serious errors 0.25/draft; core facts 92/96, detail facts 92/120 vs accuracy 4.17, coverage 3.42, actionability 3.08; serious errors 0.00/draft; core facts 94/96, detail facts 94/120
claims.note: Blind judge (`claude-opus-5-5`, not one of the models under test; 1 rubric pass per draft; each pair shown in both orders, position-consistent in 19/24 pairs); 12 drafts per cell over 4 documents; key facts from a fixed answer key. Compared under the written rule: the template against the unbounded draft on the same model, and Haiku against Sonnet on the row with the template; ties are left out of the head-to-head share. claims.claim: Prefix caching + sliding-window summary prevents quadratic session cost
claims.measured: context slope: without +1247 tok/turn (turn 10 21.9k) → with +288 tok/turn (turn 10 14.8k, peak 15.6k); cost $398.68 → $212.45 per 1k sessions billed (−47%; n=6 sessions per version); quality: recall questions 2/36 with vs 36/36 without, turn 1–3 details kept in the final summary 24/51 vs 37/51
claims.note: Rule: holds if the version with the improvement grows its context more slowly per turn and costs less per session billed. Both hold: the summaries bound the growth from turn 6 on, and the cached handbook prefix cuts the price of each turn. The cost claim holds, but the saving is not free: after compaction the early-turn specifics are no longer in the context, and replies to recall questions about them stated that the detail was not available (see the quality table and the implicit-claim row).

claims.measured: with vs without the improvement (n=6 sessions each): answers grounded (turns 1–9) 205/207 vs 205/207; recall questions 2/36 vs 36/36; turn 1–3 details in the final summary 24/51 vs 37/51
claims.note: Answer key, deterministic string matching, 95% Wilson intervals; the reference is the version without the improvement. Replies on turns 1–9 stay grounded in both versions, but once early turns are compacted, replies to recall questions about them did not give their specifics and the final summary kept fewer of them. Implicit-row rule: a clear loss (recall questions: the intervals do not overlap).

claims.claim: Pair hybrid retrieval (reranking + chunk filtering) with context caching
claims.measured: with the improvement (Haiku picks 5 clauses from the cached full corpus, Sonnet answers over them with citations; n=24 per corpus size) vs without (full corpus, no cache, no citations): expected clauses among the picks 99% / 99% (7 / 21 documents); other suppliers' clauses picked 0/120 / 0/120; $/question billed $0.0230 / $0.0250 vs $0.0459 / $0.1173 (−50% / −79%); answers with a serious error 0/24 / 2/24 vs 1/24 / 3/24
claims.note: Rule (both corpus sizes, with vs without the improvement at the same size; "clearly" = 95% Wilson intervals do not overlap): retrieval holds if the picked clauses' share of expected clauses is not clearly below the full corpus's (which holds every clause) and no other supplier's clause is picked; cost holds if it is cheaper per question billed in 8-question sessions; quality holds if its share of answers with a serious error is not clearly higher. Retrieval holds; cost holds; quality holds.

claims.measured: with vs without the improvement (7 / 21 documents, n=24 answers each): answers with a serious error 0/24 / 2/24 vs 1/24 / 3/24; grader correctness 4.75 / 4.54 vs 4.50 / 4.50; key facts 153/159 / 154/159 vs 156/159 / 150/159
claims.note: Reference: the version without the improvement (full corpus, no cache, no citations) at the same corpus size. Clear loss: the share of answers with a serious error is clearly higher (95% Wilson intervals do not overlap). No clear loss at either size. Implicit-row rule: no clear loss is detected, but point estimates are lower (7 docs: key facts 153/159 vs 156/159), and 24 answers per cell cannot show the versions are equal, so the row is PARTLY. Blind grader, one pass per answer; the deterministic key facts move less than the grader's error count.

claims.claim: Max-step budgets + deterministic guardrails + small-model routing for routine tool calls
claims.measured: max-step budgets: 0 of 108 runs hit a cap; without the lever (12-turn safety cap) runs finished in at most 4 turns, with it in 4 of 5; with vs without the lever (Sonnet): cost -67% billed ($153 → $51.22/1k; warm $153 → $30.49), turns 3.9 → 4.0, exact vouchers 36/36 → 36/36; Haiku-first vs Sonnet (with the lever): cost -80% billed ($51.22 → $10.42/1k; warm $30.49 → $5.94), exact vouchers 36/36 → 36/36, switched to Sonnet in 6 of 36 runs
claims.note: Judged as a whole, without → with, in three parts. (1) Step budgets: not shown — no loop ran long on these invoices, so a budget saved nothing here; whether it prevents runaway cost is untested. (2) Deterministic guardrails (the with-design): supported — with the lever, cost changed -67% and exact vouchers 36 → 36 of 36. The with-design also replaces the raw tables with one narrow query and sends the policy manual as a cached prefix, so the saving belongs to the design as a whole and these cells cannot split it between the guardrail and those changes. (3) Small-model routing: supported — starting on Haiku changed cost -80% against Sonnet on the same design, with exact vouchers 36 → 36 of 36; it switched to Sonnet in 6 of 36 runs, the runs where the policy tool flags a multi-factor dispute (manual 6.2). As a whole: 2 of 3 parts supported, 0 contradicted, 1 never came into play.

claims.claim: Isolate sub-agent contexts, cache the shared repo prefix, measure cost per verified outcome (CpO)
claims.measured: CpO per verified fix (billed): Without the lever: shared bus, Sonnet $0.469 (15/15 verified); With the lever: isolated + cached, Sonnet $0.100 (15/15 verified); With the lever: isolated + cached, Haiku agents + Sonnet patch author $0.056 (15/15 verified)
claims.note: On Sonnet, the lever cuts cost per verified fix ~4.7× ($0.469 → $0.100; warm $0.469 → $0.078); with Haiku agents + a Sonnet patch author it is $0.056 (~8.3× below the shared bus). The verified rate is the same in every cell, so every saving is cost per run and CpO adds nothing over it here (ceiling): the outcome side of the claim is untested.

claims.claim: Monotonic token scale: Cat 1 < Cat 2 < Cat 3 < Cat 4 < Cat 5 << Cat 6
claims.measured: Cat 1 (item) 1.5k; Cat 2 (document) 8.5k; Cat 3 (10-turn session) 169.6k; Cat 4 (4-question audit) 77.5k; Cat 4 (single question) 19.4k; Cat 4 (single question, 3× corpus) 55.1k; Cat 5 (invoice, raw tables) 75.9k; Cat 6 (incident run, shared bus) 217.8k
claims.note: 1 < 2 < {3,4,5} < 6 holds. The order of 3, 4 and 5 depends on the unit: a 10-turn session bills more than a single RAG question or a whole invoice.
